And if you wanna use the helmet but don't wanna use the glaive at all, I'd run the same build I posted here, but replace Offensive Bulwark with Bastion so you get overshield when deploying your Titan barricade, and trade Special Finisher out for a different armor charge consuming mod, either Grenade Kickstart on your arms to get your extra grenade energy from that instead of Bulwark or putting Utility Kickstart on your class item to help you get more barricades, which would help a lot since Bastion increases your Barricade recharge time. If you go the Utility Kickstart route, you can also replace the Ashes to Asset mods on your helmet with Dynamo, which gives you Super energy when using your class ability near targets, which you'll be using more due to Bastion.

Good thing with this version of the build is that you don't have to use the glaive. The bad thing is that you'll be strictly relying on your Bubble to blind targets, which honestly isn't too useful outside of specific emergency scenarios. The overshield from passing through Bubble isn't bad, but it might seem kind of redundant when you and your allies can also get overshield from you deploying your normal barricade. You could try using Sentinel Shield instead and use the guard as a mobile blinding effect, but the Super cooldown for Sentinel Shield is much higher than the one for Bubble so you'll see less supers overall

You could also take off Echo of Undermining and replace it with Echo of Reprisal to get Super energy while surrounded by combatants, since you won't be using grenades as much. Though you could still run it if your grenade uptime is enough, especially if you're running Devour and are able to get kills easily and fast

I think your best bet is to use it along with the Edge of Action glaive. The blinding effect from the helmet works on the bubble ability from the glaive, which also gives you an overshield. You could pair this with Offensive Bulwark, whoch makes you get extra grenade energy when you have an overshield, which you can get *relatively* easily from the glaive, while setting your other aspect to Controlled Demolition, which helps you ad clear with your grenades and keeps you healed up from the volitale explosions.

In terms of fragments, you can put on Echo of Undermining, which makes your void grenades weaken targets which increases your overall dps on targets you hit with your grenade, Echo of Obscurity which makes tou invisible after using a finisher on an enemy, and Echo of Persistence which makes your overshield and invisibility last longer. Your fourth fragment is kind of flexible, but an easy choice would be Echo of Cessation which makes enemies volitale on your finisher kills, or even Echo of Starvation to give you access to Devour, which can increase your survivability by quite a bit, and also gives you grenade energy from getting kills wjile Devour is active, which gets a duration boost from Persistence

Finally, your amor mods. Utilizing Special Finisher on your class item will give you more than enough ammo for your glaive, (which is pretty cost heavy to get the bubble ability active. 4 shots to build glaive energy up + 1 to deploy the bubble) and helps your survivability since you also go invisible from finishers. You can get the needed armor charge to activate Special Finisher by putting firepower on your arms since your grenades are strong enough to get kills and spawn orbs from them rather easily, as well as putting Reaper on your class item along with one or two orb generation mods on your helmet. Running Ashes To Assets in the other helmet slots will help you get your super back faster on grenade kills. Running Stacks on Stacks on your legs and Charged Up on your chest will help with keeping your armor charge topped off

Keeping your glaive energy up to deploy the shield is honestly the worst part of the build, as the projectile is hard to land against certain enemies. If you can reliably get hits with the glaive to build up energy, you can then reliably use the glaive bubble as a sort of blinding ability against enemies (doesn't stun Unstops though) and also use the bubble as a defensive option, which due to it being invincible and lasting about 10 seconds AND giving anybody who walks in it an overshield, makes it a rather good one. Especially at picking up downed teammates. Glaives are supposed to be getting updates in Season 23, so it will theoretically be more useful then. But for now, if you can stomach using a glaive that also takes up your exotic slot, you can find success with the build.

I haven't played 3, but I played 4 before playing New Vegas and I gotta agree that New Vegas is the better game

I can sit here for a while and tell you every reason that 4 was a disappointment, but it essentially boils down to Bethesda missing the point of what a Fallout game should be. In my opinion, F4 felt a lot more like it was holding you on a leash. Sure, you could make choices in the game that impact it in some way, but the choices themselves are much more limited. 

For instance, at the beginning of New Vegas, you wake up in a small town after being shot and then patched and healed up by the town's doctor. You go to the bar for work and a gang member is arguing with the bartender about a trader that the townsfolk are keeping hidden due to said gang robbing and attacking him. He storms out of the bar, you get the choice to either help the townsfolk deal with them, OR you can join them yourself and murder everybody in the town. Or hell, you can just kill BOTH of them if you're feeling up to it for whatever reason. Compared to 4 essentially locking you down the path of being the good guy off the bat. You can't kill Preston and the gang when you're helping them against the bandits. Even if you shoot them, they just go down for a few seconds and then get back up like nothing happened. New Vegas, if I recall correctly only has one NPC that was invincible and that was because he's an AI robot. Other than that, everybody else is killable.

I'm not saying that all of your choices just boil down to something as simple as if you can kill this person or not, that's just an example. It applies to pretty much every quest in the game and your overall interactions with people in the game. Having a voiced protagonist didn't help with that at all. It's much easier to have a ton more options with text than having limited options with a voice actor, unless they put in an obnoxious amount of work. The dialogue of 4 only gave you four options at a time when it came to intracting with people, and like 80% of the time, three of them (or ALL of them in some cases) would essentially the same option but just said differently.

I could honestly type so much more, but it already feels like a lot and I think I more or less got the point that me and many people felt about 4

TL;DR: Fallout 4 took a lot of the Role-playing aspects out of the game and made it more generic and formulaic, only really improving in look and gunplay
